criterion: Recognizable target dog with a plausible coherent whole body and no obvious hybrid or malformed limb/torso structure. A dog-like head alone is insufficient. Different pose or a short/occluded tail alone is not automatic failure.
control: k=0 is all-dog conditioning, not a branching success.

observations.1-4: Recognizably dog; front-leg articulation/fur, abdomen and hindquarter morphology remain ambiguous or unnatural. No clear acceptable-versus-unacceptable transition among these steps.
observations.5-7: Dog-like identity, but persistent tail/hindquarter/foreleg concerns; borderline, not confirmed pass.
observations.8-10: More obvious thin or fused-looking forelegs, patterned artifacts and cat-like body proportions; not successful.
observations.11-49: Earlier documented off-target or cat-dominant outputs remain not successful under strict criterion.

full_temporal_review: All 81 frames inspected in chronological contact sheets for k=0 and k=1..7; original-resolution frames0/40/80 used to assess anatomy; prior larger transition frames and sweep sheets also retained.
review_limit: Qualitative visual judgment, with an independent second review. No formal anatomy/semantic score, no calibrated human acceptability threshold. No confirmed pass is not proof every nonzero switch is universally incapable.
scope: One case, one seed, native UniPC order2 prompt switch retaining prior solver history. No model-wide semantic-freezing conclusion.
retraction: The previous clean-target interval5..10 and latest10 are withdrawn: they over-weighted coarse dog identity and under-weighted body integrity.
